text.p: Here are highlights from Polish newspapers this morning.
RZECZPOSPOLITA

- Poland's economy is sufferring from overheating this year but gross domestic product (GDP) will reach 6.5 percent, only 0.5 percent less than last year, economic experts at the Central Statistical Office (GUS) and the Polish Academy of Sciences (PAN) said.
- Fiat Auto Poland will start selling a modernised version of the Fiat 126 elx model equipped with a catalytic converter.
The car will be offered in two versions: a standard one worth 11,920 zlotys and an elegant one for 13,070 zlotys.
- Japanese Mazda 121 cars will be imported to Poland within EU duty-free quotas next year.
The car is made in the UK-based Dagenham plant.
- Around 100 investors and local and foreign corporate executives are participating in the Economist Group's two-day conference in Warsaw on Poland's investment opportunities.
- Plus GSM mobile phone subscribers have recently faced problems in connecting with the TPSA-operated regular telecom network, caused by an overload of newly subscribed GSM phones.
The mobile phone firm promised to set up more than ten base stations in the Warsaw area in near future.
- The Tymbark SA juice maker has a 6.5 percent share in Poland's juice market.
The plant's output has grown by 2,300 percent in the last five years, the company said.
- The Kielce-based Browar Kielce wants to increase its output to two million hectolitres annually, the company said.
- The annual net profit of the American Express Poland credit card issuing firm in 1995 was 391,000 zlotys, the company said.
NOWA EUROPA
- Banks are not intersted in crediting the bankrupt Gdansk shipyard despite the government's readiness to guarantee the credits.
- Local and foreign investors are ready to invest over one million dollars in the Katowice Special Economic Zone (SEZ).
The brunt of investments will come from Toyota and two Japanese banks.
- The DuPont Conocco Poland fuel distributor will have opened 19 petrol stations around the country by year-end, the company said.
- Trade unions in the Elblag-based ABB Zamech plant have demanded a 24-percent pay rise in place of the 15-percent rise offered by management.
- Fiat Auto Poland sold 16,500 Fiat Punto cars by the end of November, making it the year's best-selling foreign car.
GAZETA WYBORCZA
- Listed bank Amerbank's revenues in November were at 4.6 milion zlotys and its net profit reached 793,800 zlotys.
- The listed Debica tyre company's November revenues were 52.1 million zlotys and net profit 1.1 million zlotys.
ZYCIE
- National Investment Fund (NFI) No. 4's investment portfolio grew by 44 percent in the first six months of this year compared with the same period in 1996.
- Poland's current account deficit will reach $11 billion next year, the planning ministry (CUP) said.
-- Warsaw Newsroom +48 22 653 9700
